CUPRUM  METALLICUM.

Copper.  Cu.

A  substance  little  known  as  a  remedy  before  Hahnemann,  although  used  by
Medijeval  physicians,  alter  its  introduction  by  Hohenheim  (called  Paracelsus)  in
the  sixteenth  century,  and  later  (1845)  in  an  empiric  way  by  the  Eademacherian
School,  in  which  it  ranked  as  a  polychrest.

A  comprehensive  monograph,  including  the  provings  and  observations  of
Hahnemann  and  his  provers,  Bonninghausen,  Stapf,  Kiickert,  etc.,  with  results  of
poisoning  and  curative  symptoms,  was  published  by  C.  Hering.  In  it  the  effects
of  the  metal  and  the  acetate  are  conjoined,  on  account  of  their  similarity,  but  sep-
arated here,  for  the  sake  of  individuality.     See  Cuprum  acetleum.
